title: An Empirical Investigation of a Digital Platform’s Release Strategy for Serialized Content
authors: Clarice Zhao; Nitin Mehta; Mengze Shi
eligible_reason: No DiD or event-study design. The paper estimates a structural two-stage (platform visit, chapter purchase) latent-segment demand model for serialized e-books in MATLAB (Tables 7-8, main_tab7_fixed.m, main_tab8.m) and motivates it with reduced-form OLS in Tables 3-6 (table1_6.pdf): daily purchases on chapter updates / past-3-day updates and a weekend dummy, consumption rate on last purchase size, purchase on previous consumption rate, and visits on updates and lagged visits. All regressors are continuous release-speed or behavioural measures; no binary treatment switching on at unit-specific dates.
design_notes: Book-reader-day purchase panel (14.5M rows per README_data_variable.docx), 138 books, chapter publishing records. Release-strategy counterfactuals come from the structural model with a control-function correction.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: reduced-form OLS on continuous release-speed and behavioural regressors; no treatment timing
